One agent plans, another executes, a third verifies my autonomous team that never complains.

7 min read
1 hour ago

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

I remember the day my single-agent AI system gave me a beautifully formatted, completely wrong answer with absolute confidence. It planned the architecture, wrote the code, and reviewed its own work — all in one prompt. And it never once questioned whether it was on the right track.
That’s when I realized the problem wasn’t the model. It was the architecture. A single agent is a jack-of-all-trades, master of none; as the complexity of its instructions grows, adherence to specific rules degrades, and error rates compound.
So I built a multi-agent system. One agent plans, another executes, a third verifies. They talk to each other, delegate tasks, and catch each other’s mistakes — just like a real team. And the results are staggering. Anthropic reports that multi-agent systems are 90.2% better than single-agent systems at complex tasks.
Here’s exactly how I built it.
